title: Allegations, evidentiary sufficiency, and persuasion
summary: A claim passes through different tests as litigation proceeds. Pleading concerns sufficient allegations; the production burden concerns enough evidence for a reasonable verdict; persuasion concerns whether the factfinder is convinced under the governing standard.
notes: Do not use a trial evidentiary checklist as an automatic pleading requirement, or assume that surviving a Rule 12 motion supplies evidence sufficient for Rule 56.

sections.Meaning: A claim passes through different tests as litigation proceeds. Pleading concerns sufficient allegations; the production burden concerns enough evidence for a reasonable verdict; persuasion concerns whether the factfinder is convinced under the governing standard.
sections.How to work through the question: For every motion, identify the stage and permissible materials. A complaint may survive dismissal and still fail after discovery. A party may produce enough evidence to reach a jury yet lose when that jury evaluates credibility and weight.
